manifests.title: Distance locus animation
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: Completing squares converts general quadratic expressions into center-radius form and reveals whether the relation is a circle, a point, or an empty set. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Define loci by distance conditions and derive the standard circle equation.

manifests.title: Center-radius equation diagram
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for conics as loci and the circle foundation.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Define loci by distance conditions and derive the standard circle equation.

manifests.title: General-form completion-of-squares panel
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why to forget that the center coordinates appear with opposite signs inside the squared factors leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Define loci by distance conditions and derive the standard circle equation.

manifests.title: Focus-directrix distance construction
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: The sign of p determines opening direction. The focus and directrix are equally distant from the vertex on opposite sides. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Derive and analyze parabolas as points equidistant from a focus and directrix.

manifests.title: Vertical and horizontal standard forms
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for parabolas from focus and directrix.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Derive and analyze parabolas as points equidistant from a focus and directrix.

manifests.title: Reflective-ray property diagram
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why to use p rather than 4p as the coefficient or to place the directrix on the same side as the focus leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Derive and analyze parabolas as points equidistant from a focus and directrix.

manifests.title: String-and-pins ellipse locus
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: The circle is the special case c=0 and a=b. As c approaches a, the ellipse becomes more elongated. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Analyze ellipses from constant-sum distance and standard equations.

manifests.title: Axis/focus parameter map
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for ellipses.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Analyze ellipses from constant-sum distance and standard equations.

manifests.title: Circle-to-ellipse comparison
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why placing the foci using b instead of c or assuming the larger denominator always belongs under x leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Analyze ellipses from constant-sum distance and standard equations.

manifests.title: Constant-difference locus
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: Asymptotes pass through the center and follow the diagonals of the fundamental rectangle with semiaxes a and b. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Analyze hyperbolas from constant-difference distance and standard equations.

manifests.title: Fundamental rectangle and asymptotes
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for hyperbolas.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Analyze hyperbolas from constant-difference distance and standard equations.

manifests.title: Horizontal-versus-vertical form comparison
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why using the ellipse relation c^2=a^2-b^2 or orienting the branches by the larger denominator rather than the positive term leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Analyze hyperbolas from constant-difference distance and standard equations.

manifests.title: Two-variable completion ledger
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: Both variable groups and the equation’s right side must remain balanced. The final constant determines scale and may reveal a degenerate or empty relation. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Convert general quadratic relations to standard conic form by completing squares.

manifests.title: Geometric square-completion blocks
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for completing squares in two variables.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Convert general quadratic relations to standard conic form by completing squares.

manifests.title: General-to-standard transformation
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why adding a completion term inside a factored group without multiplying its contribution correctly on the other side leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Convert general quadratic relations to standard conic form by completing squares.

manifests.title: Classification decision matrix
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: Completing squares provides center or vertex translations. Dividing by the final constant normalizes the equation to standard form. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Classify translated conics and recover all geometric features from standard form.

manifests.title: Translated coordinate axes
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for translated conics and general equations.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Classify translated conics and recover all geometric features from standard form.

manifests.title: Coefficient-sign comparison
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why classifying solely from the larger coefficient or denominator while ignoring sign and normalization leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Classify translated conics and recover all geometric features from standard form.

manifests.title: Degenerate conic gallery
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: A circle form with squared radius zero gives one point; a negative squared radius gives no real points. Similar threshold behavior occurs in ellipses and hyperbolas. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify point, line, pair-of-lines, empty-set, and other degenerate quadratic relations.

manifests.title: Parameter threshold from ordinary to degenerate
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for degenerate conics and classification.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify point, line, pair-of-lines, empty-set, and other degenerate quadratic relations.

manifests.title: Algebraic factorization of line pairs
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why forcing every quadratic equation into the name of a nondegenerate conic leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify point, line, pair-of-lines, empty-set, and other degenerate quadratic relations.

manifests.title: Focus-directrix ratio construction
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: For standard ellipses and hyperbolas, e=c/a. Increasing e stretches an ellipse toward a parabola and opens a hyperbola more strongly relative to its vertex distance. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use eccentricity to compare circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.

manifests.title: Eccentricity family morph
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for eccentricity and unified conic structure.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use eccentricity to compare circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.

manifests.title: Parameter ranges by conic type
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why using b/a or confusing the directrix distance with the focal distance c leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use eccentricity to compare circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.

manifests.title: Conic intersection gallery
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: The resulting polynomial degree predicts possible intersection counts. Repeated roots often indicate tangency, while nonreal roots indicate no real intersection. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve and interpret intersections of lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas.

manifests.title: Subtract-to-eliminate squared terms
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for nonlinear systems involving conics.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve and interpret intersections of lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas.

manifests.title: Tangency and multiplicity comparison
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why pairing each recovered x-value with every y-value rather than preserving the correct substitution relation leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve and interpret intersections of lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas.

manifests.title: Parabolic reflector ray diagram
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. Materials, loading, thickness, measurement error, and three-dimensional effects limit the model. The calculation and the representation should agree, so a graph, diagram, table, or substitution check should support the same conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct and critique conic models in reflection, orbit, architecture, and navigation settings.

manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct and critique conic models in reflection, orbit, architecture, and navigation settings.
